45169.title: Authorizer change is rejected by the API while a non-voided invoice exists

before.custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in to ShopView. You also need a way to send a request to the system directly, outside the screens - a developer or the automation engineer will have this.
2. You need a work order that has been invoiced and has not been voided or reversed. To reach it: click "Work Orders" in the top menu and open the work order.
3. You need the customer to have a contact who approves work. To check or set that: click "Customers" in the top menu, open the customer, click the "Contacts" tab, click the edit icon on a contact's row and tick "Approves Work".
4. This case deliberately checks the back end rather than the screen: on screen the Authorizer is already locked once the work order is invoiced, and the point here is that the lock also holds when the screen is bypassed.
before.custom_steps:
1. Click "Work Orders" in the top menu and open the invoiced work order, so you can see the Authorizer row in the customer card on the left and note the name it currently shows.
2. Send a change-authorizer request to the system directly, bypassing the screen: POST /api/work-orders/change-authorizer with body {"workOrderId": "<the work order id>", "authorizerContactId": "<the id of a contact who approves work>"}.
3. Read the response the system gives back.
4. Return to the work order in the app, reload it, and look at the Authorizer row again.

provenance: This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-8218 and story SV-9142 (Story 3, Order Reference Fields) and the Invoice UI Refresh specification version 45, section S3-R5, read on 31 August 2026.

45185.title: A snapshot created before the redesign renders in the new layout with blanks and no error

before.custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in to ShopView.
2. You need a work order that was invoiced BEFORE this version was built - check the dates in its history.
3. To open a saved copy of a document: click "Work Orders" in the top menu, open the work order, and open its History. The entries that keep a saved copy are "Invoice created", "Invoice downloaded", "Invoice emailed" and "Reviewed"; open the saved copy from one of those entries.
4. For comparison you also want a saved copy made today: click "Work Orders", open a work order that is Complete, click its "Finance" tab and create an invoice, then open the History entry that appears.
before.custom_steps:
1. Click "Work Orders" in the top menu, open the old work order, and open its History.
2. Open the saved copy of the document from an entry dated before this version was built.
3. Check that the document opens at all, and that no error message appears in place of it.
4. Read its layout, then save or print it and read that too.
5. Look at the fields that did not exist when that copy was made - the Authorizer, the licence plate, the estimate date - and check whether they are simply left blank rather than showing an error.
